case.subject: Unilever logistics and order management
case.problem: Global supply chains struggle with 'messy' incoming orders—discrepancies in product codes, pricing, or shipping data—which historically required manual staff intervention to investigate and correct, causing significant delays in transaction processing.
case.workflow: Unilever deployed a multi-agent system where autonomous agents ingest incoming orders and cross-reference them against internal inventory and pricing databases. If an order contains a mismatch, the agent flags it, retrieves the necessary context from historical logs, and proposes a corrected transaction. Human supply chain managers retain final authority, reviewing the agent's proposed fix and the supporting evidence before approving the transaction for fulfillment.
case.result: The agents transition previously stalled, manual reconciliation tasks into checked, ready-to-process transactions, reducing the cognitive load on human staff who only intervene to approve exceptions.
case.result_basis: Microsoft corporate case study; UK Stories feature
case.measurement_context: Qualitative improvement in order throughput and reduction in manual intervention; Unilever reports efficiency gains in processing messy transactional data.
case.limitation: The system's efficacy relies on the accuracy of the underlying master data and historical transaction logs; complex exceptions still require human expertise.
case.listener_action: Identify the 'messy' data bottleneck in your department where someone manually corrects the same error daily; ask if your existing systems allow for an agent-based reconciliation pilot.
case.availability: Generally available within the Microsoft Copilot agent framework.
